properties.title: Sliders Camp
properties.thought: End of day one.

properties.title: Suspension reality check
properties.thought: Day one and already wondering if the load is too much — that bump stop is not resting on the frame, but it is close.
properties.photoCaption: Not much travel left in this suspension.

properties.title: East Port Bay Road, Wolcott, NY
properties.thought: End of day two. Camped near Wolcott.

properties.title: Roney Road, Wolcott, NY
properties.thought: End of day three.

properties.title: Adjala-Tosorontio, ON, Canada
properties.thought: End of day four. Into Canada!

properties.title: Neyaashiinigmiing Reserve, ON, Canada
properties.thought: End of day five.

properties.title: Lighthouse on Georgian Bay
properties.thought: This old lighthouse has been watching over Georgian Bay for more than a century.
properties.photoCaption: A weathered red-capped lighthouse stands sentinel over the grey waters of Georgian Bay.

properties.title: Gauthier's Road, Assiginack, ON, Canada
properties.thought: End of day six.

properties.title: Bruce Peninsula National Park
properties.thought: Into Bruce Peninsula National Park — one of Canada's most dramatic landscapes.
properties.photoCaption: Parks Canada entrance sign for Bruce Peninsula National Park of Canada.

properties.title: Niagara Escarpment Cliffs, Bruce Peninsula
properties.thought: These sheer dolomite cliffs over Georgian Bay might be the most dramatic thing I've seen so far.
properties.photoCaption: Sheer dolomite cliffs of Bruce Peninsula drop into the turquoise waters of Georgian Bay.

properties.title: Chi-Cheemaun Ferry, Tobermory
properties.thought: Boarding the Chi-Cheemaun to cross Georgian Bay — the 'Big Canoe' lives up to its name.
properties.photoCaption: The Chi-Cheemaun Ontario ferry, adorned with Indigenous artwork, prepares to cross Georgian Bay.

properties.title: Black Creek, ON, Canada
properties.thought: Screen room deployed — such is life in the boreal where mosquitoes rule.
properties.photoCaption: Settled in for the night, screen room is the Navigator's first line of defense.

properties.title: Rabbit Blanket Lake, ON, Canada
properties.thought: End of day eight.

properties.title: Foggy Shoreline, Lake Superior Provincial Park
properties.thought: Lake Superior generates its own weather — fog rolling in mid-afternoon.
properties.photoCaption: Fog drifts across a rocky Lake Superior shoreline, conifers dissolving into grey.

properties.title: Highway 35, ON, Canada
properties.thought: End of day nine.

properties.title: Boreal Lake, Lake Superior Provincial Park
properties.thought: The boreal has a way of making every lake look like the only lake in the world.
properties.photoCaption: Mirror-calm boreal lake with lone island, surrounded by black spruce and reflected sky.

properties.title: Pukaskwa National Park
properties.thought: Pukaskwa — one of Canada's least-visited national parks, and wild as they come.
properties.photoCaption: Entrance sign at Pukaskwa National Park of Canada, gateway to wild Lake Superior country.

properties.title: Driftwood Beach, Lake Superior
properties.thought: Lake Superior's shores are decorated with years of driftwood — raw and beautiful.
properties.photoCaption: Driftwood-strewn sandy beach on the shores of Lake Superior near Pukaskwa.

properties.title: Sleeping Giant Provincial Park, ON, Canada
properties.thought: End of day ten.

properties.title: Arnold's Campground, International Falls, MN
properties.thought: End of day eleven.

properties.title: Sleeping Giant Provincial Park Cliffs
properties.thought: The Sleeping Giant's cliffs drop straight into Superior like the edge of the world.
properties.photoCaption: Sheer cliffs of Sleeping Giant Provincial Park plunge into Lake Superior, a small island visible through the haze.

properties.title: Grahams Island State Park, Poplar Grove, ND
properties.thought: End of day twelve.

properties.title: Svenson Creek, Prairie County, MT
properties.thought: End of day thirteen. Deep in the Montana plains.

properties.title: Montana Badlands Road
properties.thought: The road just keeps going — Montana plays by its own scale.
properties.photoCaption: A gravel track arrow-straight through the Montana badlands, mesa rising in the distance.

properties.title: Pine Creek Road, Livingston, MT
properties.thought: End of day fourteen. Livingston with the Absarokas on the horizon.

properties.title: Missoula, MT
properties.thought: End of day fifteen. Missoula earns its reputation.

properties.title: Missoula, MT
properties.thought: A rest day in Missoula — no complaints.

properties.title: Lochsa River, ID
properties.thought: End of day seventeen. The Lochsa is running clear and cold.

properties.title: Timbren bump stop upgrade -- an on the road suspension hack.
properties.thought: The Timbrens brought my stance back to near level. Should get us to the Arctic.
properties.photoCaption: Timbrens to bring me back to a near level stance.

properties.title: Lochsa River, ID
properties.thought: The Lochsa runs cold and clear — this is what wild rivers look like.
properties.photoCaption: The crystal-clear Lochsa River tumbles over boulders through Idaho's dense conifer forest.

properties.title: Pink House Campground, Clearwater County, ID
properties.thought: End of day eighteen. Clearwater country.

properties.title: Cutthroat on the Lochsa
properties.thought: Cutthroat on the Lochsa — Navigator couldn't resist making a few casts.
properties.photoCaption: A fat cutthroat trout from the Lochsa River, hooked and ready to go back.

properties.title: Burbank, WA
properties.thought: End of day nineteen. Into Washington.

properties.title: Poppy's Red Shed Fly Shop, Lewiston, ID
properties.thought: Worth the effort to find this iconic fly shop. The Navigator's first pilgrimage to the Red Shed.
properties.photoCaption: The Navigator's first pilgrimage to the Red Shed Fly Shop.

properties.title: Ice Harbor, WA
properties.thought: Awning out, habitat module deployed, forest quiet — this is exactly why we do this.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo fully deployed under the conifers — awning extended, kitchen set up, habitat module ready.

properties.title: Skunk Creek, Grays Harbor County, WA
properties.thought: End of day twenty-one. Deep in the Olympic Peninsula.

properties.title: Mount Rainier National Park Entrance
properties.thought: Through the gates of Rainier — the mountain gods are watching.
properties.photoCaption: Timber arch entrance gate to Mount Rainier National Park, firs dripping green behind.

properties.title: Alpine Valley, Mount Rainier NP
properties.thought: That valley view from Rainier's flanks is the kind of thing that resets everything.
properties.photoCaption: Deep alpine valley on the flanks of Mount Rainier, winding road visible far below.

properties.title: Willaby Campground, WA
properties.thought: End of day twenty-two. Lake Quinault is extraordinary.

properties.title: Quinault Rain Forest, Olympic Peninsula
properties.thought: The Quinault rainforest doesn't let you rush — it's too alive for that.
properties.photoCaption: Fog-filled old-growth rainforest near Quinault, moss draped over every surface.

properties.title: Willaby Campground, WA
properties.thought: End of day twenty-three. Another night at Willaby.

properties.title: Lake Quinault Sunset
properties.thought: Lake Quinault at sunset — I could stay here for a week.
properties.photoCaption: Golden sunset over Lake Quinault, silhouetted firs and driftwood framing the calm water.

properties.title: Willaby Campground, WA
properties.thought: End of day twenty-four. Another night at Quinault.

properties.title: Willaby Campground, WA
properties.thought: End of day twenty-five. Still at Willaby — no complaints.

properties.title: Colonel Bob Wilderness Sign
properties.thought: The Colonel Bob Wilderness — where the old-growth still holds court.
properties.photoCaption: Carved wooden boundary sign for Colonel Bob Wilderness, Olympic National Forest.

properties.title: Summit of Colonel Bob
properties.thought: Summit of Colonel Bob — 360 degrees of Olympic Peninsula wilderness.
properties.photoCaption: The Navigator's companions on the rocky summit of Colonel Bob, Olympic Mountains spreading to every horizon.

properties.title: Mora Camp, Olympic NP, WA
properties.thought: End of day twenty-six. The Hoh coast is something else.

properties.title: Olympic Coast Tide Flats
properties.thought: Low tide on the Olympic coast — getting low to see what the sea reveals.
properties.photoCaption: Navigator looking for the perfect shot of the Olympic tide flats, telephoto lens trained on sea life below.

properties.title: Tide Pool Life, Olympic Coast
properties.thought: The tide pools on the Olympic coast are a whole universe at knee height.
properties.photoCaption: Macro shot of a purple sea urchin and sea star in a crystal-clear Olympic Peninsula tide pool.

properties.title: Mora Campground, Olympic NP, WA
properties.thought: End of day twenty-seven. Quillayute River at the doorstep.

properties.title: Hurricane Ridge, Olympic NP, WA
properties.thought: End of day twenty-eight. High above the Peninsula.

properties.title: Quinsam Campground, Campbell River, BC
properties.thought: End of day twenty-nine. Into BC via ferry.

properties.title: MV Coho Ferry, Port Angeles
properties.thought: Aboard the Coho — bound for Victoria and the northern miles ahead.
properties.photoCaption: Flags of Canada, the US, and Black Ball Line fly as the MV Coho departs Port Angeles for Victoria, BC.

properties.title: Campbell River, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty. Island highway north.

properties.title: Telegraph Cove, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty-one. Telegraph Cove is worth every kilometre.

properties.title: BC Logging Truck, Vancouver Island
properties.thought: Logging trucks own the roads up here — this one filled the whole lane.
properties.photoCaption: A loaded BC logging truck fills the narrow forest road ahead, Waldo's CarPlay tracking every twist.

properties.title: Blackfish Sound, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty-two. Orca country.

properties.title: Orca in Blackfish Sound
properties.thought: An orca surfacing in Johnstone Strait — this is why the route goes here.
properties.photoCaption: An orca surfaces in Blackfish Sound, blow spray catching the light, forested BC coast behind.

properties.title: An epic day to reach Side Bay, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty-three. Remote northern Vancouver Island.

properties.title: View from the habitat module, Side Bay
properties.thought: The view from the habitat module at Side Bay — this is what the hard driving is for.
properties.photoCaption: View from inside the habitat module at Side Bay, BC — a tidal inlet and snow-capped peaks framed by the open hatch.

properties.title: Waldo on Side Bay Beach
properties.thought: Spotting scope out on the Side Bay beach -- scanning for sea otter and transient orcas.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo parked on the gravel beach at Side Bay, BC, spotting scope deployed and scanning the water.

properties.title: Side Bay, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty-four. Fog and quiet.

properties.title: Rocky Shore, Side Bay
properties.thought: Low tide at Side Bay — every rock shows something worth looking at.
properties.photoCaption: Enjoying the kelp-strewn rocky shore at Side Bay, BC, mountains rising across the inlet.

properties.title: San Josef, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty-five. The end of the road on northern Vancouver Island.

properties.title: San Josef Bay Campsite, BC
properties.thought: Waldo earned every speck of that mud — habitat module up, awning out, San Josef Bay delivered.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo arrives at San Josef Bay campsite, caked in mud, habitat module up and awning deployed in the BC rainforest.

properties.title: Port Hardy, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty-seven. Preparing for the big float.

properties.title: Rocky BC Outer Coast
properties.thought: Scrambling the rocky outcrops at the tip of Vancouver Island — this coastline is otherworldly.
properties.photoCaption: Surveying the island-studded BC outer coast from the rocky shore near San Josef Bay.

properties.title: Prince Rupert, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty-eight. Prince Rupert via BC Ferries.

properties.title: BC Ferries, Port Hardy to Prince Rupert
properties.thought: Boarding the ferry at dawn for the 16 hr trip to Prince Rupert — Waldo gets the day off.
properties.photoCaption: The bow doors open on the BC Ferries vessel at Port Hardy, loading for the long run to Prince Rupert.

properties.title: Motz Road, BC
properties.thought: End of day thirty-nine. Heading inland from the coast.

properties.title: Lavergne Road, BC
properties.thought: End of day forty. Skeena country.

properties.title: Elizabeth Lake, Kispiox, BC
properties.thought: Scanning Elizabeth Lake from the habitat module at first light — the wildlife comes out when the camp stays quiet.
properties.photoCaption: Looking for (and finding!) loons at first light.

properties.title: Jigsaw Lake Recreation Site, BC
properties.thought: Jigsaw Lake — the kind of spot that makes you recalibrate what 'beautiful' means.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo lakeside at Jigsaw Lake Recreation Site, BC. Co-Navigator watching loons.

properties.title: An overland rigs party overlooking Salmon Glacier
properties.thought: The Salmon Glacier viewpoint draws rigs from all walks of life — Waldo camped here with a collection of wanderers from around the world.
properties.photoCaption: Overland rigs, campers and expedition vehicles parked for the night at the Salmon Glacier viewpoint at dusk.

properties.title: Grizzly Tracks, Hannah Creek
properties.thought: Fresh grizzly tracks in the mud along Hannah Creek — we weren't the only ones on this road today.
properties.photoCaption: Fresh grizzly bear tracks pressed deep in the mud along Hannah Creek near Meziadin Junction.

properties.title: Waldo at Salmon Glacier Viewpoint
properties.thought: Waldo at the Salmon Glacier viewpoint — the scale of it doesn't register until you're standing there.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo parked at the Salmon Glacier summit viewpoint, the massive blue-white glacier filling the valley below.

properties.title: Glacial Bar Camp, Hyder, AK
properties.thought: End of day forty-four. Crossed into Alaska — barely.

properties.title: Shrimp Tacos, Stewart, BC
properties.thought: Shrimp tacos in Stewart — civilization appears in unexpected places.
properties.photoCaption: Shrimp tacos served on a cedar board in Stewart, BC — a surprisingly excellent restaurant at the end of the road.

properties.title: Bear on Fish Creek, Hyder
properties.thought: Fish Creek delivers — a grizzly with a salmon in its mouth.
properties.photoCaption: A grizzly bear works a salmon in Fish Creek near Hyder, AK — the salmon run was on.

properties.title: Glacial Bar Camp, BC
properties.thought: Camped on the glacial bar with fog threading the mountains — this is Waldo in its element.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo set up on a glacial gravel bar in BC, milky turquoise river in front and fog-wrapped mountains behind.

properties.title: Kinaskan Lake Campground, BC
properties.thought: End of day forty-six. Kinaskan Lake glows at dusk.

properties.title: Teslin Lake Campground, YT
properties.thought: End of day forty-seven. The Yukon begins.

properties.title: Teslin Lake Provincial Park, YT
properties.thought: End of day forty-eight. Yukon country.

properties.title: Yukon Welcome Sign -- starting to feel like the Arctic.
properties.thought: The Yukon sign — stickers from a thousand journeys before ours.
properties.photoCaption: The Yukon welcome sign covered in travel stickers, its murals depicting the rivers, mountains, and spirit of the territory.

properties.title: Chilcoot River Campground, YT
properties.thought: End of day forty-nine. The Chilkoot corridor.

properties.title: A quick detour back into Alaska to look for bears.
properties.thought: Welcome to Alaska — for real this time. The gateway to the Klondike.
properties.photoCaption: Welcome to Alaska and the Gateway to the Klondike — the border sign at White Pass in alpine glory.

properties.title: Grizzly on the Chilkoot River, AK
properties.thought: A grizzly on the Chilkoot coming straight at the lens — that's a good use of a telephoto.
properties.photoCaption: A soaking wet grizzly bear strides along the rocks of the Chilkoot River near Haines, AK, heading straight for the camera.

properties.title: Chilkoot Lake, AK
properties.thought: End of day fifty. Halfway to Tuk.

properties.title: Kathleen Lake Campground, YT
properties.thought: End of day fifty-one.

properties.title: Fireweed and Yukon Peaks
properties.thought: Fireweed in August means summer is turning — and the mountains don't care.
properties.photoCaption: Fireweed in full bloom frames snow-capped Yukon peaks, summer's last hurrah before the alpine turns gold.

properties.title: Donjek River Camp, YT
properties.thought: Camped on a braided glacier bar in the Yukon — blue sky, no fences, just mountains.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo fully deployed on the Donjek River bar, snow-capped peaks of the St. Elias Range looming behind.

properties.title: Kathleen Lake Reflection, YT
properties.thought: Kathleen Lake in the Yukon has no right to be this perfect.
properties.photoCaption: Kathleen Lake in perfect reflection — a conical Yukon peak and cirrus sky mirrored in crystal-clear water.

properties.title: Eagle Trail Rec Site, AK
properties.thought: End of day fifty-three.

properties.title: End of Nabesna Road, Wrangell-St. Elias NP, AK
properties.thought: End of day fifty-four. Into the biggest national park in the US.

properties.title: Alpine Tundra Hike, Wrangell-St. Elias
properties.thought: Wrangell-St. Elias doesn't mess around — the rocks are serious and the tundra is already turning.
properties.photoCaption: A hiker climbs through early-fall alpine tundra in Wrangell-St. Elias NP, jagged granite towers looming above the valley.

properties.title: Aurora at the start of Top of the World Highway, YT
properties.thought: The Top of the World Highway starts here — and the aurora showed up to mark the occasion.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo's habitat module silhouetted against a full aurora borealis display over the Top of the World Highway.

properties.title: Back into Canada on the Top of the World Highway, YT
properties.thought: End of day fifty-six. Next stop -- Dawson City to the Dempster Highway.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo on a Dempster ridgeline, vast fall-toned Yukon mountains stretching to every horizon under deep blue sky.

properties.title: Waldo on Taylor Mountain
properties.thought: A tiny black speck on the side of Taylor Mountain — Waldo and the Yukon on equal terms.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo navigates the descent of Taylor Mountain across fall tundra in full color, the Yukon's infinite ridgelines receding behind.

properties.title: Chicken, Alaska
properties.thought: Chicken, Alaska — the rooster and the signpost say it all.
properties.photoCaption: The famous metal rooster and directional signpost in Chicken, Alaska, pointing to chicken-named places worldwide.

properties.title: wild camp on the North Klondike River, YT
properties.thought: End of day fifty-seven. North Klondike River.

properties.title: George Black Cable Ferry, Dawson City
properties.thought: The George Black ferry at Dawson City — a cable ferry across the Yukon, running on river current alone.
properties.photoCaption: The George Black cable ferry crosses the Yukon River at Dawson City, fall birch turning yellow on the far bank.

properties.title: Dempster Highway Sign, Dawson City
properties.thought: Dempster Highway 5 North — Arctic Ocean 880km. There it is on a sign.
properties.photoCaption: Dempster Highway 5 North at Dawson City: Eagle Lodge 363km, Inuvik 735km, Arctic Ocean 880km.

properties.title: Blackstone River Camp, YT
properties.thought: End of day fifty-eight. The Dempster unwinds north.

properties.title: Tombstone Range from the Ridge
properties.thought: Standing above Tombstone Park's valley — those dark spires live rent-free in your head forever.
properties.photoCaption: co-Navigator looks out from an alpine ridge over the jagged Tombstone peaks and glacial valley, Yukon.

properties.title: Eagle Plains, YT
properties.thought: End of day fifty-nine. Eagle Plains — the only stop for a hundred miles.

properties.title: Eagle Plains Fuel Stop
properties.thought: Eagle Plains — the only diesel for 200 km in either direction. Top it off, always.
properties.photoCaption: Fueling up at Eagle Plains, the Dempster's only gas station for hundreds of kilometres.

properties.title: Gwich'in Territorial Campground, NT
properties.thought: End of day sixty. Crossed the Arctic Circle.

properties.title: 'Watch for Aircraft' Sign, Dempster
properties.thought: Only on the Dempster — watch for planes landing on the road.
properties.photoCaption: 'Watch for Aircraft Landing on Highway' — a Dempster original, where bush pilots share the gravel strip with trucks.

properties.title: Arctic Circle Monument
properties.thought: LAT 66° 33 N — the Arctic Circle on the Dempster. That's real.
properties.photoCaption: The Arctic Circle monument at Lat 66° 33 N on the Dempster Highway, vast tundra rolling to the horizon.

properties.title: Muskox on Arctic Tundra
properties.thought: First muskox — they look exactly like what came out of the last ice age.
properties.photoCaption: A solitary muskox stands on the Arctic tundra of the Dempster corridor, staring down the camera.

properties.title: Dempster Sunset
properties.thought: The Dempster sunset doesn't negotiate — it just burns.
properties.photoCaption: Fiery sunset over the fall tundra of the Dempster Highway, burnt spruce silhouettes and a sky on fire.

properties.title: Tuktoyaktuk, NT, Canada
properties.thought: The Arctic Ocean. Made it.
properties.photoCaption: Two travelers at the Tuktoyaktuk welcome sign — the end of a 61-day journey from Pennsylvania to the Arctic Ocean.

properties.title: This is what easy conditions look like on the Dempster Highway.
properties.thought: Nearing the end of the Dempster — and the beginning of the road into Tuk.
properties.photoCaption: This is what 880 kilometers to the Arctic Ocean looks like on the Dempster Highway.

properties.title: The Arctic Ocean, Tuktoyaktuk
properties.thought: The Arctic Ocean at Tuktoyaktuk. The front bumper dipped in.
properties.photoCaption: Waldo's hood and bumper frame the Beaufort Sea at Tuktoyaktuk — the Arctic Ocean at journey's end.
